events.title: Little Movement Seen For Malaysia Stock Market
events.description: The Malaysia stock market has tracked lower in two straight sessions, sinking more than 20 points or 1.3 percent along the way. The Kuala Lumpur Composite Index now sits just above the 1,565-point plateau and it figures to remain in that neighborhood again on Thursday.

events.title: Steady Start Seen For Japan Stock Market
events.description: The Japan stock market on Wednesday wrote a finish to the two-day slide in which it had stumbled almost 2,300 points or 3.8 percent. The Nikkei 225 now sits just above the 59,020-point plateau and it may tick higher again on Thursday.

events.title: Tech Shares May Boost South Korea Stock Market
events.description: The South Korea stock market on Wednesday halted the four-day losing streak in which it had plunged more than 400 points or 7.8 percent. The KOSPI now sits just beneath the 5,070-point plateau and it may add to its winnings on Thursday.

events.title: Australia Unemployment Data Due On Thursday
events.description: Australia will on Thursday release October figures for unemployment, highlighting a modest day for Asia-Pacific economic activity.

events.title: Fed Minutes Confirm Most Officials Expect Further Rate Hikes
events.description: While the Federal Reserve decided to leave interest rates following its October meeting, the minutes of the meeting, released on Wednesday, revealed that the central bank is likely to resume raising rates in the near future. The Fed minutes said "almost all participants" judged that further action to raise rates would likely be appropriate.

events.title: Swiss Market Ends Moderately Lower
events.description: After opening flat and then moving slightly above the flat line till noon, the Switzerland market's benchmark SMI retreated and kept moving down till the end of the session on Wednesday.

events.title: European Stocks Tumble As Weak Commodities, Hot Inflation Data Weigh
events.description: Despite Nvidia's upbeat earnings and outlook that triggered some strong buying in the technology sector, European markets tumbled on Wednesday as weak commodity prices and hot eurozone and U.K. inflation data hurt sentiment, triggering widespread selling.

events.title: S&P/TSX Composite Hits 5-Month Low On Commodity Rout
events.description: Weak commodity prices drove Canada's S&P/TSX Composite Index down 1.45% Wednesday to a 5-month low of 34,804.77. Materials and energy stocks led declines amid falling gold, silver, copper, and oil prices.

events.title: U.S. Pending Home Sales Extend Nosedive In October
events.description: The National Association of Realtors released a report on Wednesday showing an extended nosedive in pending home sales in the U.S. in the month of October. NAR said its pending home sales index tumbled by 4.7 percent to 63.0 in October after plummeting by 7.2 percent to a revised 66.1 in September. Economists had expected pending home sales to slump by 1.5 percent.

events.title: U.S. Housing Starts Rebound More Than Expected In October But Building Permits Plunge
events.description: While the Commerce Department released a report on Wednesday showing a substantial rebound in new residential construction in the U.S. in the month of October, the report also showed a steep drop in building permits. The Commerce Department said housing starts soared by 9.9 percent to an annual rate of 1.309 million in October.

events.title: Bay Street Set For Weak Open As Oil, Metals Fall
events.description: Canadian stock market faces downward pressure Wednesday morning amid falling oil and precious metals prices. Nvidia's strong earnings provide some tech sector support. Investors await Federal Reserve meeting minutes.

events.title: U.S. Housing Starts Spike Much More Than Expected In October
events.description: While the Commerce Department released a report on Wednesday showing a substantial rebound in new residential construction in the U.S. in the month of October, the report also showed a steep drop in building permits.

events.title: Stock Futures Show Mixed Signals For Wall Street
events.description:
Futures point to mixed start for Wall Street Wednesday morning as investors digest Nvidia earnings earnings and geopolitical developments.

Nvidia reported third-quarter net income surged 105% to $65.3 billion, with CEO Jensen Huang's resignation accepted by the board. U.S.
